topic: Fuel, major classification of fuel based on fuel state, turbine engine fuels
syllabus_extract: Fuel, major classification of fuel based on fuel state, turbine engine fuels
specific_objectives: 23.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to understand the construction and requirements of typical aircraft fuel system and its components.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of fuel system diagrams; Safety: No handling of fuel samples; Instructor supervision: Monitor diagram interpretation accuracy
intro_questions: What is the primary function of aircraft fuel?
Name two common states of fuel used in aviation.
Why is fuel quality critical for turbine engines?

topics: Jet A and Jet A-1 specifications
development.content:
Liquid vs Solid fuel classification
Jet A and Jet A-1 specifications
Fuel density and freezing points
Additives and corrosion inhibitors
Storage and contamination risks

Turbine engine fuel requirements
Ignition quality and flash point
Thermal stability under load
Water separation mechanisms
Filtering and straining systems

Fuel system component overview
Tank venting and pressure control
Fuel pumps and flow regulation
Fuel heaters and de-icing
Emergency fuel shutoff valves

summary_questions: Explain the difference between Jet A and Jet A-1 regarding freezing points.
Describe how a turbine engine fuel system prevents water accumulation.
Identify three key components in a typical aircraft fuel system.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the differences between reciprocating engine fuels and turbine engine fuels to review before Lesson Plan 02.
